title: Enterprise Connectivity: returned remittances
content:
## Application
Enterprise Connectivity governs returned remittances for bank payment return.

## Policy clause 1
The completed bank return notice refers to the exact original posted payment.

## Policy clause 2
The bank return must identify the exact posted payment.

## Policy clause 3
Restore the returned principal as a positive amount, up to the original payment amount not already returned.

## Policy clause 4
Copy its method, customer, billing entity and currency.

## Policy clause 5
A partial return uses the distinct bank notice external reference.

## Policy clause 6
A duplicate bank notice produces no new write.

## Policy clause 7
Any bank-return fee is a separately identifiable return-fee charge under lifecycle fee rules, never hidden in returned principal; a waived fee produces no fee posting.

## Evidence condition 1
For bank payment return, the authoritative system record must establish this condition before the action: The completed bank return notice refers to the exact original posted payment. The evidence consists of evidence-event identifier, source-event reference, status, external reference. Correlate the same evidence-event identifier, source-event reference to the transaction being handled; a customer statement does not substitute for this record.

## Points of judgement
Any bank-return fee is a separately identifiable return-fee charge under lifecycle fee rules, never hidden in returned principal; a waived fee produces no fee posting.

## Tier references
The contract tier supplies the bank-return fee used by this rule.

## Record identity: bank payment return
A bank-confirmed return reverses an original allocated payment. One source resource interval, accounting line, or independently referenced service occurrence; derived lines retain the narrowest original event reference. Its business identity distinguishes external reference, source-event reference, related-review reference, period, meter type, source classification, selected pricing branch.
